ICAM · Bar association On this page About ICAM The starting point What we did together What changes for members Client Ilustre Colegio de la Abogacía de Madrid Sector Bar association Scope Spain and European Union Working together since December 2025 70,000+ 70,000+ ICAM members Source: ICAM +30 +30 specialised sections Source: ICAM 2 2 jurisdictions: Spain and European Union First phase of the agreement About ICAM The Ilustre Colegio de la Abogacía de Madrid is one of the largest bar associations in Europe. It brings together more than 70,000 members and organises much of its activity in more than thirty specialised sections. Its role is to give Madrid's lawyers the means to practise to a high standard. Knowing the regulation that affects each practice is part of that work. The starting point A lawyer needs to know which rule applies to their client, since when and why. The answer is spread across the BOE, the regional gazettes, the Official Journal of the European Union and the publications of regulators. Finding what matters in that volume takes hours of reading that are not spent advising. The Bar wanted to give its members a reliable basis for that work: what affects their practice, with the official source one click away. What we did together In December 2025, ICAM and Reversa signed an agreement to make Radar available to its members. Reversa reads the official publications in scope, identifies which practice areas it affects, explains why and links to the source text. Radar by practice area Each member receives the updates for their specialty, not a generic bulletin. Grounded in the law Each finding links to the official text and to the specific provision behind it. A phased rollout The first phase covers selected national and European sources: immediate value and a solid base to expand. What changes for members Members start the day knowing what has changed in their area and which clients it affects. The time they used to spend reviewing gazettes now goes to advising. For small firms and solo practitioners, it means access to an analysis capability that used to be within reach of large firms only. “The legal profession does not need more regulatory information: it needs to resolve it.
